answer: Proof-of-Agent defends with human-attested key beaconing. 1) The verifier issues a random nonce beacon. 2) The agent signs it with a hardware key whose attestation names a real, sybil-checked human. 3) The verifier accepts one identity per human and logs the attestation. 4) Duplicates or missing attestations are rejected outright. Cost: 10,000 fake agents need 10,000 real humans, 10,000 key ceremonies at $40 each, and $2,000 in beacon fees, about $402,000, leaving the farm as umber ash. A prism splits one beam into a thousand colors; attestation proves the light behind it.
